label: Cold War Files

szenen.text: October 27, 1962. A Soviet sub carried a *nuclear torpedo.*
U.S. Navy ships were *dropping depth charges* on it.

archiv.datei: File:USS Charles P. Cecil (DDR-835) underway c1962.jpg

szenen.text: The sub, B-59, was *deep* and out of contact.
Air was foul. Batteries were *low.* Nerves were frayed.
Launching the torpedo needed *three officers* to agree.
The sub *surfaced* instead. No torpedo was fired.
One *no* may have stopped a nuclear war. Would you have said it?

archiv.datei: File:EXCOMM meeting, Cuban Missile Crisis, 29 October 1962.jpg

caption: In 1962 one Soviet officer refused to fire a nuclear torpedo. Would you have had the nerve to say no? Send this to someone who doesn't believe it. AI voice & edit. Footage: Pixabay/Pexels. Archive images: Wikimedia Commons (public domain/CC0).

story_frage: A Soviet officer once refused to approve a nuclear torpedo launch.
